mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates weakening labor market conditions, which often precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDPC1, or if the correlation between GDPC1 growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates supply-side constraints, which can lead to inflationary pressures and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO drops and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it indicates a tightening monetary environment with inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) show a significant decline and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises, it signals a weakening labor market, which often precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS drops > 100k in 1 month and UNRATE rises > 0.3pp
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a rise in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a shift in consumer spending from durable goods to services, which can signal a weakening economic demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops > 10% in 1 month and RSAFS rises > 1%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is stagnant and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising, it suggests a supply-side constrained economy with tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO flat or drops < 1% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of INDPRO stagnation and FEDFUNDS increases on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
